description: The mid-stream read failure: two records are read and displayed, the third READ reports '23', and the run abends inside 1000-CARDFILE-GET-NEXT - so CARDFILE is never closed and the end banner is never written. Six lines out, and the arithmetic of the case is deliberately asymmetric: "inputs" seeds THREE rows and "expectedMessages" carries only TWO 150-character images. That gap is the whole claim: a translation that pre-read its input, buffered it, or flushed what it had already fetched would emit a third image here that the COBOL does not. The three rows are written out inline, so the row that is never read is visible in the case file rather than implied. Two neighbours come close and neither makes this statement. case14 seeds three fixture rows and fails after all three, so its input is exhausted and it can say nothing at all about an unread row. case20 does leave a row behind, but it names its two rows as a fixture window rather than writing them out, and its second read reports a response with no two-character equivalent, so it lands on the extended '9' arm of 9910 rather than on the numeric one - a different assertion on both counts. This one fails strictly mid-stream: past the first read, short of the last row, over an input small enough to take in at a glance. THE SEQUENCE, in emission order. :71 writes the start banner. The mainline at :74-81 then runs PERFORM 1000-CARDFILE-GET-NEXT followed by the guarded DISPLAY CARD-RECORD at :78, twice: the first READ at :93 reports '00', :95 moves 0 into APPL-RESULT, :104 IF APPL-AOK continues, control returns to the mainline, :77 finds END-OF-FILE still 'N' and :78 writes row 1; the second read repeats it for row 2. The third READ reports '23'. '23' is neither '00' nor '10', so :101 moves 12 into APPL-RESULT; :104 IF APPL-AOK is false and :107 IF APPL-EOF is false, because APPL-EOF is the 88-level for 16 and this is 12; so the ELSE at :109-113 runs in source order - :110 DISPLAY 'ERROR READING CARDFILE', :111 MOVE CARDFILE-STATUS TO IO-STATUS, :112 PERFORM 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS, :113 PERFORM 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM, which at :155 writes 'ABENDING PROGRAM' and at :158 CALLs 'CEE3ABD' and does not return. WHAT IS ABSENT, AND WHY BOTH ABSENCES ARE ASSERTIONS. There is no third image, even though the third row is sitting in the dataset: the DISPLAY is at :78 in the MAINLINE, after the PERFORM at :76 has already returned, and the abend at :113 is inside the performed paragraph - so control never reaches :78 a third time. The guard at :77 is IF END-OF-FILE = 'N' and not "if a record came back", which is why a '23' read - one that delivers nothing at all - is indistinguishable at :78 from one that never happened. And there is no 'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBACT02C' line, because :83 PERFORM 9000-CARDFILE-CLOSE and :85 DISPLAY both sit past the abend: the browse is left open, the CLOSE never runs, and its own :139 status test is never evaluated on this path. A translation that wrapped the pass in a finally-style release and then carried on to the banner would emit a seventh line and fail here. THE RETURN CODE. APPL-RESULT holds 12 at the moment of the abend, from :101, so expectedReturnCode is 12 - carried out to the step as the batch exit status, which is what makes a JCL COND test on a following step behave as it does today (gate G35). The 8 that :119 moves before the OPEN is transient and never observable, and the 16 of :99 is the APPL-EOF marker rather than a return code, so the only two values this program can end with are 0 and 12. 999 is the ABCODE from :157 and 0 is the TIMING from :156 - the two arguments CEE3ABD reads. They are named here and nowhere else in the case, because they are not the RETURN-CODE and putting either in expectedReturnCode would assert the wrong number; AbendException carries all three and AccountBalanceReaderJobTest pins them against it. WHY ONE 'OTHER' STATUS SUFFICES FOR THE ARM. The test at :94-103 is three-way and this case drives its third arm: '00' -> 0 -> APPL-AOK -> continue, '10' -> 16 -> APPL-EOF -> orderly end of file, and ANYTHING ELSE -> 12 -> the abend path. CBACT02C treats every non-'00', non-'10' status identically; the status value changes only the four digits 9910 renders and never the control flow. So the arm needs one case per rendering, not one per status, and this directory spends them accordingly - '22' on the first read in case12, an untranslatable response on the first read in case13 and after one record in case20, and '23' after three records in case14. THE STATUS LINE, AND THE NNNN THAT REALLY IS THERE. '23' is numeric and its first byte is '2' rather than '9', so 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS takes the ELSE arm - branch (b) at :170-172: MOVE '0000' TO IO-STATUS-04, then MOVE IO-STATUS TO IO-STATUS-04(3:2), leaving the image '0023'. :172 then DISPLAYs the literal 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' followed by that image with no separator between them, so the emitted line is the twenty-character literal - whose last four characters genuinely are the letters NNNN, an unsubstituted editing template left in the source - plus four digits, twenty-four characters in total: FILE STATUS IS: NNNN0023. It is reproduced verbatim and must never be tidied to 'FILE STATUS IS: 0023' or to a space-separated form; preserving an inherited defect is the point of a parity gate (practice B5). HOW THE FAILURE IS INDUCED, AND HOW IT IS NOT. ParityCase.ForcedOutcome is the model's affordance for a per-call-site I/O outcome, but it hangs off ScreenRequest and ParityCase refuses a screenRequest on a BATCH_JOB case - a batch job has no screen - so this file cannot declare the failing read as data, and inventing a member for it would break all 560 fixtures. The complete expected fingerprint is therefore declared here, and the run shape is wired by parity/CBACT02CParityTest, whose Scenario.forCase maps case17 to a read that delivers two rows and then reports NOT_FOUND. Named precisely, for gate G47: openBrowse reported '00', the first and second readNext reported '00', the THIRD readNext reports '23', and endBrowse is never reached. What must NOT be attempted is inducing the failure with a short or malformed row: FixedWidthCodec.padToDeclaredWidth widens a short row on the right with spaces and rejects only an over-long one, so a truncated row would be silently repaired to 150 bytes and produce a SUCCESSFUL read - the case would then assert the wrong thing entirely. That is a verified property of the codec, recorded here so nobody retries the approach; the reference fixture is read-only either way (practice B3). THE ROWS AND THEIR GEOMETRY. The three rows are rows 1, 2 and 3 of app/data/ASCII/carddata.txt - byte-identical to the classpath copy at src/test/resources/fixtures/carddata.txt - written inline and verbatim, in ascending CARD-NUM order, so the row the third read would have returned is visible in the case rather than implied: 0500024453765740 (Aniya Von, 2023-03-09), 0683586198171516 (Ward Jones, 2025-07-13) and 0923877193247330 (Enrico Rosenbaum, 2024-08-11). Each is exactly 150 characters, which app/cpy/CVACT02Y.cpy declares as CARD-NUM X(16) at 1-16, CARD-ACCT-ID 9(11) at 17-27, CARD-CVV-CD 9(03) at 28-30, CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME X(50) at 31-80, CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE X(10) at 81-90 - misspelled in the copybook and carried through unchanged, because a renamed field cannot be diffed field for field - CARD-ACTIVE-STATUS X(01) at 91 and FILLER X(59) at 92-150. DISPLAY CARD-RECORD at :78 names the 01 group item, so each emitted line is the whole area including that FILLER, and the two images therefore end in fifty-nine spaces: a codec that dropped the FILLER would emit 91 characters and a codec that mis-sized any field would shift every byte after it (gates G19 and G21). :96 is a commented-out second DISPLAY and contributes nothing - one image per record, never two. THE REST OF THE FINGERPRINT. jobParameters is empty because app/jcl/READCARD.jcl:22 is a bare EXEC PGM=CBACT02C with no PARM and the program has no LINKAGE SECTION to receive one into. expectedWrites and expectedFinalState are empty as positive assertions, not omissions: :120 opens CARDFILE INPUT and the program contains no WRITE, REWRITE or DELETE, and FieldDiffer traverses each channel in both directions, so an empty expectation is the statement that nothing was written. normalisations is empty because carddata.txt is already at its copybook width - neither recorded fixture deviation touches it. The dataset is addressed only through its binding key CARDFILE, the DD at app/jcl/READCARD.jcl:25; the fully-qualified dataset name that DD resolves to at :26 stays in configuration and is written neither here nor in Java, and ParityCase's dataset-key pattern is narrow enough that a dotted, fully-qualified name could not pass validation even if one were (gate G46). The code page is named explicitly as US-ASCII rather than taken from the platform (practice B8). The unit is driven at tasklet level with no JobLauncher, no context and no HTTP in the path (gate G51). THE NAME DIVERGES FROM THE BEHAVIOUR. The unit is account.AccountBalanceReaderJob, an "Account"-named class in the account package, but CBACT02C reads the CARD file: :29 SELECTs CARDFILE, COPY CVACT02Y at :45 brings in the 150-byte card record, and app/jcl/READCARD.jcl:25-26 binds the DD to the card master. It computes no balance and writes nothing. Rule R1 of the plan governs - the name comes from the prompt and the behaviour comes from the source - and register 0.8.4 lists this among sixteen like it. The divergence is documented and preserved, never corrected. PROVENANCE. Every expected value above was STATICALLY DERIVED by structured reading of app/cbl/CBACT02C.cbl paragraph by paragraph, cross-checked against app/cpy/CVACT02Y.cpy for the byte layout, app/jcl/READCARD.jcl for the step and the absence of a PARM, and the real app/data/ASCII/carddata.txt for the rows. It was NEVER captured from a live COBOL run: running the legacy programs is impossible in this environment, for the eight independently verified blockers recorded in Agent Action Plan section 0.7.6 - no z/OS runtime, an indexed file handler reported disabled by the only available compiler, which alone rules out :30 ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED, no Language Environment CEE* service for the CALL at :158, and five more. Provenance is the only thing that changed; twenty cases, field-by-field diffing and a diff count that must be zero all survive intact. This is risk R-A, escalated rather than absorbed (practice B12). review_rules reports no user rules for this project, which is not licence to lower the bar: the binding standard is the plan's enterprise practice set, and the gates this case pins are G15, G18, G19, G21, G35, G47 and G51.
